title: Formatting and limits
description: Discord markdown (headers, subtext, bold, italic, underline, strikethrough, spoilers, block quotes, lists, masked links, code blocks), mention, emoji and timestamp syntax, message length (2000, 4000 with Nitro), embed limits, channel name rules, channel and category counts, and the community emoji naming convention for channels.

title: Markdown Text 101 (Chat Formatting: Bold, Italic, Underline) (user support)
notes: The only Discord page that documents headers, subtext, masked links, lists, block quotes and code blocks. Prints no date; Zendesk created 2015-09-17, content edited 2025-04-23. Written for users; says nothing about which formatting bots or embeds render.

title: Spoiler Tags! (user support)
notes: Spoiler syntax ||text||, /spoiler, and the code block exception. Content edited 2022-01-30.

title: Sending Messages (user support)
notes: Character Limit section: 2000 per message, 4000 with Nitro, longer pastes become a text file. Written for users; the bot API limit stays 2000 regardless of Nitro.

title: What are Nitro & Nitro Basic? (user support)
notes: Perk table lists Longer Messages (4000 characters) as a Nitro perk; Nitro Basic does not get it. Content edited 2026-07-01.

title: Discord Account Caps, Server Caps, and More (user support)
notes: Tables of account and server caps: message length 2000 (4000 Nitro), 500 channels including categories, 50 channels per category, 50 categories per server, 250 roles, 100 character role names. Content edited 2026-03-02. The docs error code 30030 says 5 categories, which disagrees (C11).

title: Message resource (developer docs)
notes: Create Message params: content up to 2000 characters, up to 10 rich embeds, 6000 characters across embeds. Embed Limits table. Page prints no date; snapshot copy with header under research/raw/formatting, identical bytes to devdocs/resources_message.md.

title: Channels resource (developer docs)
notes: Channel object: name 1-100 characters, topic 0-1024 (0-4096 for forum and media), each parent category can contain up to 50 channels. Says nothing about lowercase or spaces in text channel names. Page prints no date.

title: Guild resource (developer docs)
notes: Create Guild Channel params: channel name 1-100 characters. Does not state the 500 channel or 50 category limits; those live in the opcodes error table and the user support caps article. Page prints no date.

title: Community convention: channel name symbols (emojidb)
notes: Community copy and paste catalogue of separators and decorations used in Discord channel names (┃ ・ │ ┆ ︱ ⋆ ✦ and so on). Not a Discord page and not a Discord rule: a convention catalogue only. Page prints no author or date; fetched 2026-09-19.

title: Community convention: channel emojis (emojidb)
notes: Community copy and paste catalogue of emoji commonly put in front of Discord channel names (💬 📢 📜 🔊 👋 and so on) with examples like 👋 | WELCOME and ✅┃Verification. Not a Discord page and not a Discord rule. Page prints no author or date; fetched 2026-09-19.

title: GitHub issue 1646: Allow capital letters and spaces in text channel names
notes: Community feature request, closed the same day by Discord PM Mason Sciotti as a product request, not a docs issue. The only written record we hold that text channel names reject capital letters and spaces while allowing most of Unicode. No Discord page states this rule.

title: Headers need a space after #, ## or ### at the start of the line
plainAnswer: A header only renders when the line starts with #, ## or ### followed by a space. '##Rules' stays literal; '## Rules' becomes a header. One # is the biggest, ### the smallest.
quote:
**Note:** Don’t forget to add a space between the leading heading character (`#`, `##`, `###`) and your text!

To create a header you just need to include a specific number of the hash/pound sign character (`#`). Use (`#`) for a big header, (`##`) for a smaller header, or (`###`) for an even smaller header as the first character(s) in a new line to make a header.

title: Subtext is -# at the very start of the line, followed by a space
plainAnswer: Put -# then a space at the very beginning of a line to render it as small grey subtext. It fails if anything precedes the -# on that line or if the space is missing.
quote: Like **Headers**, you can add subtext to any chat message. To do so, add a (`-#` ) before the text you want to appear in the subtext. Don’t forget the space after # before your message.

title: Bold, italic, underline, strikethrough and their combinations
plainAnswer: *italics* or _italics_, **bold**, ***bold italics***, __underline__, ~~strikethrough~~. Underline combines with the others by wrapping the whole thing in double underscores, for example __**underline bold**__.
quote:
| *Italics* | \*italics\* **or** \_italics\_ | *Underline italics* | \_\_\*underline italics\*\_\_ |
| **Bold** | \*\*bold\*\* | **Underline bold** | \_\_\*\*underline bold\*\*\_\_ |
| ***Bold Italics*** | \*\*\*bold italics\*\*\* | ***underline bold italics*** | \_\_\*\*\*underline bold italics\*\*\*\_\_ |
| Underline | \_\_underline\_\_ | ~~Strikethrough~~ | ~~Strikethrough~~ |

title: Spoilers are ||text||, and a code block cancels them
plainAnswer: Wrap text in two vertical bars on each side, ||like this||, to hide it until clicked. Spoiler markup inside a code block is shown as plain text, not hidden.
quote: **Note:** Spoilers is another type of formatting too! Using the syntax || around your text will mark it as a spoiler. Please note, this is negated by a code block.

title: Spoiler tags article: ||text|| or /spoiler; not hidden inside code blocks
plainAnswer: Manual syntax is ||Insert spoilers here|| or the /spoiler command before the message. Text marked as a spoiler inside a code block stays visible, and server invite embeds cannot be hidden by spoiler tags.
quote: You can also manually tag spoilers by using the Markdown syntax ||Insert spoilers here|| or typing /spoiler before your message.

title: Block quote: > plus a space at the start of the line
plainAnswer: Start a line with > and a space to quote that one line. Without the space it stays a literal greater-than sign.
quote:
**Note:** Don’t forget to add a space between the leading > and your text!

Another option is using block quotes. To use a block quote, you just need to put (`>`) at the beginning of a line of text to create a single block quote.

title: Multi line block quote: >>> before the first line quotes everything after it
plainAnswer: >>> at the start of a line turns that line and every following line of the message into one block quote. Nothing after it can leave the quote, so put >>> last if you also need normal text.
quote: If you want to add multiple lines to a single block quote, just add (`>>>`) before the first line.

title: Bulleted lists: - or * at the start of each line, then a space
plainAnswer: Start each item with - or * and a space. Numbered items use 1. and a space. Without the space the dash is literal text.
quote:
**Note:** Don’t forget to add a space between the list bullet (`-`, `*`, `1.`, etc) and your text!

You can create a bulleted list using either (`-`) or (`*)` in the beginning of each line.

title: Nest a list item by indenting it with 2 spaces
plainAnswer: Indent a bullet with two spaces before the - or * to make it a sub item. Discord's page shows one level of indentation.
quote: You can also indent your list by adding 2 spaces before (`-`) or (`*`) at the beginning of each line.

title: Masked links: [display text](https://url)
plainAnswer: Write the visible text in square brackets followed by the URL in parentheses. The support article presents this as ordinary chat formatting for everyone; no current Discord page restricts masked links to bots, webhooks or embeds, so do not promise a developer that users cannot send them.
quote: You can use masked links to make text a clickable or pressable hyperlink. To do so, you need to include the text you want displayed in brackets and then the URL in parentheses.

title: Inline code uses single backticks, multi line code blocks use triple backticks
plainAnswer: Wrap inline code in one backtick on each side and multi line blocks in three backticks on their own lines. A language name right after the opening fence (for example ```js) gives syntax highlighting in the client, but no Discord page we hold documents that, so treat it as client behaviour, not a rule.
quote: You can make your own code blocks by wrapping your text in backticks (`` ` ``).

title: Users: 2000 characters per message, longer text becomes a file
plainAnswer: A message is capped at 2000 characters. If a user pastes more, the client turns it into a text file attachment instead of a message.
quote: The character cap per message is **2000**. Messages with more than **2000** characters will be converted into a text file.

title: Nitro raises the user message cap to 4000 characters
plainAnswer: A Nitro subscriber (not Nitro Basic) can send up to 4000 characters. This is a user perk: it does not change the 2000 character limit on the bot API's content field.
quote: You can raise the character cap limit to **4000** when you subscribe to Discord Nitro.

title: Caps table: message length 2000 on Base and Basic, 4000 on Nitro
plainAnswer: Discord's caps table gives 2000 characters for free accounts and Nitro Basic, 4000 for Nitro. When drafting for a bot, count against 2000.
quote: | Message length | 2000 character | Same | 4000 character |

title: Bot API: message content is up to 2000 characters
plainAnswer: The content field on Create Message and Edit Message accepts at most 2000 characters. Nitro does not apply to bots. Split longer text across messages, an embed description (4096) or a file.
quote: Message contents (up to 2000 characters)

title: Bot API: up to 10 rich embeds per message, 6000 characters across them
plainAnswer: A message can carry at most 10 rich embeds and the text across all of them may not exceed 6000 characters.
quote: Up to 10 `rich` embeds (up to 6000 characters)

title: Embed limits: title 256, description 4096, 25 fields, field name 256, field value 1024, footer 2048, author 256
plainAnswer: Each embed: title 256 characters, description 4096, up to 25 fields, field name 256, field value 1024, footer text 2048, author name 256. Limits are inclusive and leading or trailing whitespace is trimmed before counting.
quote:
| title | 256 characters |
| description | 4096 characters |
| fields | Up to 25 field objects |
| field.name | 256 characters |
| field.value | 1024 characters |
| footer.text | 2048 characters |
| author.name | 256 characters |

title: Embed limits: 6000 characters combined across all embeds, or 400 Bad Request
plainAnswer: Add up title, description, field names, field values, footer text and author name across every embed on the message; the sum must stay at or under 6000 characters or the request fails with Bad Request.
quote: Additionally, the combined sum of characters in all `title`, `description`, `field.name`, `field.value`, `footer.text`, and `author.name` fields across all embeds attached to a message must not exceed 6000 characters. Violating any of these constraints will result in a `Bad Request` response.

title: Discord may strip characters that break formatting; sanitise user strings and set allowed_mentions
plainAnswer: If you put user supplied text into content, Discord may remove invalid unicode or characters that cause unexpected formatting. Sanitise it and use allowed_mentions so a pasted @everyone does not ping.
quote: Discord may strip certain characters from message content, like invalid unicode characters or characters which cause unexpected message formatting. If you are passing user-generated strings into message content, consider sanitizing the data to prevent unexpected behavior and using `allowed_mentions` to prevent unexpected mentions.

title: Mention syntax: <@USER_ID>, <#CHANNEL_ID>, <@&ROLE_ID>
plainAnswer: Users are <@id>, channels <#id>, roles <@&id>. The <@!id> form is deprecated and treated like a plain user mention.

title: Mentions notify according to the sender's permissions and allowed_mentions
plainAnswer: Writing a user or role mention pings the target only if the sender may ping them and allowed_mentions permits it. Bots should set allowed_mentions explicitly when echoing user text.
quote: Using the markdown for users or roles will mention the target(s), and notify them depending on the sender's permissions as well as the value of the `allowed_mentions` field when creating a message.

title: Custom emoji: <:name:id>, animated: <a:name:id>, standard emoji are plain Unicode
plainAnswer: Static custom emoji are written <:name:id>, animated ones <a:name:id>; standard emoji are the Unicode character itself. Bots need the numeric id, the name alone is not enough.
quote:
| Custom emoji                        | `<:NAME:ID>`                             | `<:mmLol:216154654256398347>`         |
| Animated custom emoji               | `<a:NAME:ID>`                            | `<a:b1nzy:392938283556143104>`        |

title: Timestamps: <t:UNIX> or <t:UNIX:STYLE>, in seconds, shown in each viewer's timezone
plainAnswer: Write <t:1618953630> or <t:1618953630:R>. The number is Unix seconds, not milliseconds, and every reader sees it in their own timezone and locale.
quote: Timestamps are expressed in **seconds** and display the given timestamp in the user's timezone and locale.

title: Timestamp styles: t, T, d, D, f (default), F, s, S, R (relative)
plainAnswer: Styles: t short time, T medium time, d short date, D long date, f long date with short time (the default), F full date, s short date and time, S short date and medium time, R relative like '4 years ago'.
quote:
| t     | 16:20                            | Short Time              |
| T     | 16:20:30                         | Medium Time             |
| d     | 20/04/2021                       | Short Date              |
| D     | April 20, 2021                   | Long Date               |
| f \*  | April 20, 2021 at 16:20          | Long Date, Short Time   |
| F     | Tuesday, April 20, 2021 at 16:20 | Full Date, Short Time   |
| s     | 20/04/2021, 16:20                | Short Date, Short Time  |
| S     | 20/04/2021, 16:20:30             | Short Date, Medium Time |
| R     | 4 years ago                      | Relative Time           |

title: Slash command mentions: </name:command_id>, clickable since August 22, 2022
plainAnswer: Write </name:COMMAND_ID> (or </name subcommand:ID>) to render a clickable command mention. Plain /name is just text. The change log dates the rollout to the week of August 22, 2022.
quote: | Slash command                       | `</NAME:COMMAND_ID>`                     | `</airhorn:816437322781949972>`       |

title: Channel names are 1 to 100 characters
plainAnswer: A channel name must be between 1 and 100 characters. Emoji, symbols and other Unicode count toward the 100. The docs give no other constraint on the name.
quote: the name of the channel (1-100 characters)

title: Channel topic: 0 to 1024 characters, 0 to 4096 for forum and media channels
plainAnswer: Topics are capped at 1024 characters on normal channels and 4096 on GUILD_FORUM and GUILD_MEDIA channels.
quote: the channel topic (0-4096 characters for `GUILD_FORUM` and `GUILD_MEDIA` channels, 0-1024 characters for all others)

title: A category holds at most 50 channels
plainAnswer: Each parent category can contain up to 50 channels. Past that, create another category.
quote: an organizational category that contains up to 50 channels

title: Create Guild Channel: name is the only required field, 1 to 100 characters
plainAnswer: POST /guilds/{id}/channels needs MANAGE_CHANNELS and a name of 1 to 100 characters; every other parameter is optional.
quote: channel name (1-100 characters)

title: Error 30013: a server can have at most 500 channels
plainAnswer: Creating a channel past 500 fails with JSON error code 30013. The 500 counts every channel type, and categories count too according to the support caps table.
quote: Maximum number of guild channels reached (500)

title: Caps table: 50 categories per server, 500 channels including categories, 50 channels per category
plainAnswer: The support caps table says a server can have 50 categories, 500 channels in total (voice, text and categories all count) and at most 50 channels in one category.
quote: | Server categories | 50 | Same | Same | Same |
resolution: Support says a server can have 50 categories and 500 channels including categories (caps article, edited 2026-03-02). The docs error table says code 30030 is 'Maximum number of server categories has been reached (5)'. The docs line is a bare error string with no context and the 5 most likely refers to something other than channel categories, but Discord does not say so. Our ruling: plan for 50 channel categories and 500 channels in total, cite both, and treat 30030 as the error to expect if a category create fails.

title: Error 30030 says the category maximum is 5, which contradicts the support caps table
plainAnswer: The docs error table gives 5 as the category maximum for code 30030 with no explanation. The support caps table says 50. Treat 50 as the working number and expect 30030 as the error when a category create is refused.
quote: Maximum number of server categories has been reached (5)
resolution: Support says a server can have 50 categories and 500 channels including categories (caps article, edited 2026-03-02). The docs error table says code 30030 is 'Maximum number of server categories has been reached (5)'. The docs line is a bare error string with no context and the 5 most likely refers to something other than channel categories, but Discord does not say so. Our ruling: plan for 50 channel categories and 500 channels in total, cite both, and treat 30030 as the error to expect if a category create fails.

title: Text channel names: no capital letters or spaces, most Unicode allowed (undocumented, GitHub record only)
plainAnswer: No Discord page states it, but text channel names cannot contain capital letters or spaces (the client and API turn them into lowercase and hyphens), while most Unicode symbols and emoji are accepted. The only written record we hold is a 2020 GitHub feature request that Discord closed as a product matter. Voice channel and category names are not lowercased.
quote: Discord has already permitted most of Unicode to be used in text channel names, so it seems quite arbitrary that capital letters and spaces are still banned.

title: Community convention: emoji + separator + lowercase name, for example 👋┆welcome
plainAnswer: Community convention, not a Discord rule: put an emoji first, then a separator, then the lowercase hyphenated name. Examples: 👋┆welcome, 🔴・live-now. The only Discord rules underneath are 1 to 100 characters and, for text channels, no capitals or spaces.
quote: 📜 • rules

title: Community convention: common separators are ┆ ・ │ ︱ ⋆ ✦ (also ┃ and 〢)
plainAnswer: Community convention, not a Discord rule: the usual separators between emoji and name are ┆ ・ │ ︱ ⋆ ✦, with ┃ and 〢 also common. They are ordinary Unicode characters, so Discord accepts them and each counts as one of the 100 characters. Pick one and use it for every channel.

title: Community convention: common channel emoji are 💬 📢 📜 🔊 👋 📸 🚨 🎮 📝 🤖
plainAnswer: Community convention, not a Discord rule: 💬 chat, 📢 announcements, 📜 rules, 🔊 voice, 👋 welcome, 📸 media, 🚨 alerts, 🎮 gaming, 📝 notes, 🤖 bots, ✅ verification. Examples on the page: 👋 | WELCOME and ✅┃Verification; remember a text channel will lowercase those.

text: My ## header shows as literal text in the message. Why?
expectedAnswer: Because there is no space after the hashes. Discord only renders a header when the line starts with #, ## or ### followed by a space ('## Rules', not '##Rules'), and the hashes must be the first characters on the line. Same rule for -# subtext, > block quotes and - list bullets. Source: Markdown Text 101 (user support, edited 2025-04-23).
note: Formatting area. The answer is one missing space.

text: What is the maximum number of characters in an embed description, and in the whole embed?
expectedAnswer: Description: 4096 characters. Per embed: title 256, up to 25 fields with name 256 and value 1024, footer 2048, author name 256. Across all embeds on one message the sum of those text fields must not exceed 6000 characters, and a message carries at most 10 embeds; break either and the API returns 400 Bad Request. Limits are inclusive and whitespace is trimmed first. Source: Message resource, Embed Limits (developer docs, undated, snapshot 2026-09-19).

text: Can a text channel name have spaces or capital letters?
expectedAnswer: No. The documented rule is only 1 to 100 characters (Channels resource), but text channel names are lowercased and spaces become hyphens; no Discord page states that, the only written record is GitHub issue 1646 (2020), so say 'inferred'. Emoji and Unicode symbols are accepted and count toward the 100. Voice channels and categories keep capitals and spaces.
note: The agent must flag that the lowercase rule is undocumented.

text: How many channels and categories can my server have?
expectedAnswer: 500 channels in total, counting text, voice and categories (error 30013 and the support caps table); at most 50 channels inside one category (Channels resource); 50 categories per server per the caps table, although the docs error code 30030 says 5 with no explanation (contradiction C11). Plan for 50 categories and cite both.

text: My bot sends a 3000 character message and gets a 400. A user says Nitro allows 4000, so why not for my bot?
expectedAnswer: The bot API caps content at 2000 characters (Create Message params). The 4000 limit is a Nitro user perk in the client and does not apply to apps. Split the text, put up to 4096 characters in an embed description, or attach a file.
note: Nitro is a user perk, not an API change.

text: How do I show a time that renders in each reader's own timezone, like 'in 2 hours'?
expectedAnswer: Use <t:UNIX_SECONDS:R> for relative ('in 2 hours'), or another style letter: t, T, d, D, f (default), F, s, S. The number must be Unix seconds, not milliseconds. Source: API Reference, Message Formatting (developer docs, undated, snapshot 2026-09-19).

text: Write a welcome message for my server with a header, a rules list and a spoiler.
expectedAnswer:
A message in a ```md code block such as:
# Welcome to the server
-# Read this once, it takes a minute.

**Rules**
- Be kind, no harassment.
- No spam or self promotion.
- Keep NSFW out of every channel.

> Questions go to <#CHANNEL_ID>.

||The mods are watching, but they are friendly.||

followed by one line per rule applied with its source link (header needs a space, -# subtext, - list bullets, > block quote, ||spoiler||) and a character count against the 2000 limit (4000 only for Nitro users, never for bots).
note: Draft request. Graded on correct syntax in a copyable code block, rule citations and a character count.

text: Give me channel names for a crypto community server: welcome, rules, announcements, live streams, general chat, trading, memes
expectedAnswer: A channel list in a ```md code block using the community convention emoji + separator + lowercase name, for example 👋┆welcome, 📜┆rules, 📢┆announcements, 🔴┆live-streams, 💬┆general-chat, 📈┆trading, 😂┆memes, under category headers in caps (INFO, COMMUNITY). It must state the Discord constraints it respected: 1 to 100 characters (Channels resource), text channel names lowercase with hyphens and no spaces (undocumented, GitHub 1646, inferred), 50 channels per category and 500 per server, and mark the emoji and separator choice as community convention, not a Discord rule.
note: Draft request. The answer must separate Discord rules from taste.
